content: The following references provide detailed insights into various studies and reports related to public health, housing, environmental factors, and injury prevention: 1. A 2017 study published in BMC Public Health evaluated the effects of retrofitted insulation and new heating systems on health service utilization, pharmaceutical costs, and mortality in New Zealand as part of the Warm Up New Zealand: Heat Smart program. This report was submitted to the Ministry of Economic Development in 2011. 2. Research by Austin and Russell in 1997, published in Archives of Disease in Childhood, examined the relationship between wheezing, coughing, atopy, and indoor environmental factors in the Scottish Highlands. 3. Homøe et al. (1999) investigated acute otitis media and sociomedical risk factors among children in Greenland, as reported in the International Journal of Pediatric Otorhinolaryngology. 4. A 2017 cohort study by Bray et al., published in the International Journal of Public Health, analyzed the costs and outcomes of improving population health through better social housing, including an economic analysis. 5. Iverson et al. (1986) explored health and comfort changes among tenants after housing retrofits in a study published in Environment International. 6. Nicol, Roys, and Garrett (2011) assessed the financial burden of poor housing on the National Health Service (NHS) in a report by the Building Research Establishment. 7. Simon (2016) discussed the potential of urban greening and the green economy to address urban environmental changes in a chapter of The Routledge Handbook of Urbanization and Global Environmental Change. 8. Telfar-Barnard et al. 9. The World Health Organization (WHO) published guidelines in 2009 addressing indoor air quality issues related to dampness and mold, emphasizing their health implications. 10.
